history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: the CSV name 'Shri Hanuman Ji Temple' is generic; this file documents Ahmedabad's most prominent Hanuman shrine, the Shree Camp Hanuman Temple in the Shahibaug Cantonment area (owned by Shri Hanumanji Mandir Camp Trust, Ahmedabad) — verify this is the intended record. Reportedly founded by Pandit Gajanan Prasad, the temple is said to be 250-300 years old and houses an idol believed to be self-manifested (swayambhu). It is one of the largest Hanuman temples in India, draws heavy crowds on Tuesdays and Saturdays, and is closely associated with soldiers given its location inside the military cantonment. In 2021 the trust proposed relocating the temple to the Sabarmati riverfront citing army security restrictions; priests and devotees opposed the move and the Tulaja Yuvak Mandal petitioned the Gujarat High Court.

town_description: Ahmedabad is Gujarat's largest city and its former capital, founded in 1411 by Sultan Ahmed Shah I on the banks of the Sabarmati river. Its walled old city became India's first UNESCO World Heritage City in 2017, known for carved wooden havelis, pols, stepwells, and Sultanate-era monuments. Today it is a major industrial and commercial hub, famous for its food culture, the Sabarmati Ashram, and as the gateway to Gujarat.

travel.road: Sadar Bazar, Shahibaug cantonment area. Inside a military-restricted zone: carry photo ID; mobiles and bags not allowed; expect a walk from the gate (reportedly ~1 km on some days - verify).
